subject: Re: ACME - Reranking model fit & validation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:12:00Z
Subject: ACME discovery recap + recommended next steps (reranking)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Primary goal: improve top-K relevance for product search on mobile (CTR and cart-add are leading metrics).
- Current baseline: production bi-encoder + simple lexical signals; customers report some headroom on reordering product lists for intent-heavy queries.
- Key constraints: 95th pctl latency budget ~200ms, sparse user history, and a hard requirement for no PII leaving ACME S3 buckets.

Recommended initial approach (what we discussed):
1) Candidate generation stays on your current bi-encoder.
2) Add a reranker powered by a lightweight cross-attention open model (we suggested a distilled Llama 2 variant quantized to int8 for cost reasons).
3) Evaluate offline with NDCG@10 and MRR, run a short A/B on 5% of live traffic with server-side fallback to current ranker.

Deliverables we committed to:
- Benchmark doc with NDCG/MRR vs baseline + per-query slice analysis (attached).
- Shared prompt set and eval harness (attached CSV and drive links).
- A mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a 6-week pilot plan (attached).

Next steps I propose:
- Connor will run the offline rerank validation on your heldout logs and share NDCG/MRR and latency distributions by Friday.
- You confirm access to a 5% production route for the A/B and any compliance or procurement steps needed.
- If the offline numbers look good, we schedule a 30-minute rollout plan next week.

Attachments: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_results.pdf (summary), acme_prompt_set_v2.csv (prompt + label pairs), ACME_mutual_action_plan.docx (MAP)

If that sounds right, I’ll mark the MAP and we can lock the pilot dates.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we move forward: 

1) For the offline eval, can you include NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR, and break results down by vertical (electronics/home/kitchen)? We care a lot about head results.
2) Latency: your suggested model (distilled Llama 2 int8) — what median and P95 token latencies should we expect on a single dedicated GPU? We have a 200ms P95 budget for the entire request.
3) A/B plan: what metrics should we use to judge success (CTR lift, add-to-cart, revenue per session)? Any recommended guardrails (fallback rules) you suggest?

Also, we’ll need a short statement of data handling for our security/compliance team: does Redwood keep logs of raw queries in the hosted flow? We might need to go Private or Dedicated depending on answers.

If you can get Connor to push the offline numbers and include the model/latency tradeoffs, we can review Wednesday.

—Samir

Subject: Re: ACME discovery recap + recommended next steps (reranking)

Hi Samir / team —

Following up with the offline validation results (summary below). Full CSV slices and the evaluation harness are in the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-rerank-evals).

Summary (holdout logs, 200k queries):
- Baseline (legacy ranker): NDCG@1=0.32, NDCG@3=0.45, NDCG@10=0.58, MRR=0.47
- Redwood reranker (distilled Llama-2-small int8, single-GPU inference): NDCG@1=0.41 (+28%), NDCG@3=0.52 (+15%), NDCG@10=0.62 (+7%), MRR=0.56 (+19%)
- Slice notes: Electronics shows the largest lift (NDCG@1 +35%), Kitchen shows marginal lift but improved tail behavior.

Latency (server-side single-token & end-to-end estimates on target instance):
- Median end-to-end per-request (avg candidate set size 12): ~85ms
- P95 end-to-end: ~170ms (within your 200ms P95 budget), with burst testing showing occasional spikes to ~220ms under synthetic stress (we recommend canarying).

A/B plan (recommended):
- Traffic: start at 5% users, escalate to 25% over 2 weeks if guardrails pass.
- Primary metric: Add-to-cart rate (expected sensitivity to reranking). Secondary: CTR and revenue/session.
- Guardrails: rollback if 95% conf. interval for add-to-cart shows negative lift > -1.5% or if P95 latency > 220ms on production.
- Fallback: if reranker fails or exceeds latency threshold, route to legacy ranker for that request only (stateless fallback).

Attachments included in Drive: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_results.pdf (filled), per_query_slices.csv, acme_prompt_set_v2.csv.

Notes on data handling (Aditya): Redwood hosted logs redact user identifiers by default in the analytics pipeline; raw query text retention is configurable per-customer. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with customer-managed retention. Aditya, can you send the short compliance blurb we usually share?

Next steps I suggest:
1) ACME confirms compliance posture and access to a 5% route.
2) Book 30-minute rollout planning meeting this week to agree on canary start date.
3) If greenlit, we schedule the 2-week pilot and provide the feature flag + monitor dashboard.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers.

Connor O'Brien
Applied ML / Inference Validation, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
